entries.topic: Aksum, Frumentius, Tewahedo church and the 81-book canon (two reckonings)

claims.text: The EOTC's English site states: 'The Ethiopian Orthodox Church has 46 books of the Old Testament and 35 books of the New Testament that will bring the total of canonized books of the Bible to 81.' Its NT list adds Sirate Tsion, Tizaz, Gitsew, Abtilis (the Sinodos), two books of Dominos (Covenant), Clement and Didascalia to the 27; its OT list includes Jubilees, Enoch, Meqabyan and Josippon ('Josephas the son of Bengorion').

Cowley 1974: the corpus is 'generally called the 81 books'; two reckonings: broader canon (traditional Amharic commentary on the Fetha Nagast) 46 OT + 35 NT = 81; narrower canon (Prayers of the Church; the large Geez-Amharic diglot and Amharic Bibles issued under the Emperor) 54 OT + 27 NT = 81, with Proverbs split into Messale and Tagsas. A variant (Kwakweha haymanot) reaches 49 + 32 = 81.
Cowley: Fetha Nagast heading says 81 'but the list does not total 81'; counted as given it holds 46 OT + 27 NT (73). Its canon section cites the Sinodos.

Cowley conclusions: narrower-canon books undisputed; broader-canon additions equally canonical from a traditionalist view but in practice treated more as commentary with derived authority; Ascension of Isaiah and Shepherd of Hermas not found to be canonical at present. Ethiopic 'Maccabees' (Meqabyan) are three books not the same as any LXX Maccabees, counted as two by the Canon Law Commentary.
Oriental Orthodox churches 'followed the teachings of the first three Ecumenical councils' (Nicaea, Constantinople, Ephesus) and reject Chalcedon.
Fetha Negest compiled in Arabic c.1240 by Abu'l-Fada'il ibn al-Assal; translated into Ge'ez in the 15th century (some records c.1450 under Zara Yaqob); supreme law until 1931.

Frumentius and Edesius of Tyre enslaved at Aksum (c.316 voyage per Rufinus); Frumentius consecrated bishop by Athanasius, traditionally 328 or 340-346; c.356 Constantius II wrote to Ezana and Saizana asking them to replace him with Theophilos; called Abba Salama and Kesate Birhan.
Ezana (r. c.320-350) converted; crescent-and-disk removed from coins and replaced with the cross; Christianity first limited to the royal elite, spreading in the later 5th century.
Garima Gospels radiocarbon: Garima 2 c.390-570, Garima 1 c.530-660 (2013 results); Niccum argues most NT translation into Ge'ez was done before end of 4th century.

EOTC: 'tewahedo' means 'made one'; rejects Chalcedon; OT originally translated into Ge'ez from the Septuagint; Nine Saints after 451; WCC figure of 60 million members; Pew c.38 million in Ethiopia (2017); 1948 agreement, Basilios consecrated 14 January 1951; Cyril VI granted autocephaly, Basilios first patriarch 1959; Eritrean autocephaly 28 September 1993; Abune Mathias sixth patriarch since February 2013; Saturday and Sunday Sabbaths accepted mid-15th century; Haile Selassie sponsored Amharic Bibles 1935 and 1960-61; Susenyos submitted to the pope 1624, abdicated 1632, Jesuits expelled 1633; Jesuit books ordered burned 1665.
Basilios installed as first Patriarch 28 June 1959 by Coptic Pope Kirillos VI in Cairo; until then the Abuna 'was always a cleric of the Coptic Church'.

Audit (22 Oct 2026) of the EOTC site list: OT 1-46 = Genesis..Ruth (8), I and II Samuel (1 entry), I and II Kings (1), I Chronicles, II Chronicles, Jublee, Enoch, Ezra and Nehemia (1), Ezra (2nd) and Ezra Sutuel (1), Tobit, Judith, Esther, I Maccabees, II and III Maccabees (1), Job, Psalms, Proverbs, Tegsats, Metsihafe Tibeb (books of wisdom), Ecclesiastes, Song of Songs, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, Daniel, twelve minor prophets (Hosea, Amos, Micah, Joel, Obadiah, Jonah, Nahum, Habakkuk, Zephaniah, Haggai, Zechariah, Malachi), Sirach, Josephas son of Bengorion; no separate Lamentations, Baruch, Letter of Jeremiah or 4 Baruch. NT 1-35: Gospels, Acts, Romans..Philemon, Hebrews, 1-2 Peter, 1-3 John, James, Jude, Revelation, Sirate Tsion, Tizaz, Gitsew, Abtilis, I and II Dominos, Clement, Didascalia.

Audit: narrower-canon OT 1-54 per the EOTC 1995 list as summarised: 1-14 Genesis..2 Chronicles, 15 Jubilees, 16 Enoch, 17 Ezra, 18 Nehemiah, 19 3 Izra (Greek Esdras), 20 Izra Sutuel, 21 Tobit, 22 Judith, 23 Esther, 24-26 1-3 Meqabyan, 27 Job, 28 Psalms, 29 Messale, 30 Tagsas, 31 Wisdom, 32 Ecclesiastes, 33 Song, 34 Sirach, 35 Isaiah, 36 Jeremiah, 37 Baruch, 38 Lamentations, 39 Letter of Jeremiah, 40 4 Baruch, 41 Ezekiel, 42 Daniel, 43-54 minor prophets Hosea..Malachi in LXX order; Prayer of Manasseh within 2 Chronicles.

Audit: Cowley places the Letter of Jeremiah (as Lam. 6) and 'the rest of the words of Baruch' (Lam. 7:6-11:63) inside Saqoqawa Eremyas; Prayer of Manasseh as 13 verses after 2 Chr 33:12; Ezra Sutu'el 13 chapters = Vulgate 4 Esdras 3-14; his 14 additions do not include additions to Esther.

entries.topic: 1 Enoch: five books, manuscripts, teachings, Jude

claims.text: 1 Enoch sections: Watchers 1-36 (older parts c.300-200 BC; Shemihazah leads 200 angels on Mount Hermon; Azazel teaches forbidden crafts; giants); Parables 37-71 (Son of Man / Righteous One / Chosen One / Messiah; most reject Milik's 3rd c. AD date); Astronomical 72-82 (Uriel; 364-day year of four 91-day seasons; Qumran copies 3rd c. BC); Dream Visions 83-90 (animal allegory of history Noah to Maccabees, c.163-142 BC); Epistle 91-108 (Apocalypse of Weeks, first half 2nd c. BC; 106-108 Noah's birth).

Manuscripts: eleven Aramaic fragments from Qumran Cave 4 (4Q201-212), Milik edition 1976, no fragments of 37-71; Greek Codex Panopolitanus (chs 1-32, 6th-c.), published 1892; Ethiopic families of 15th-18th c. manuscripts; Charles 1906 used 23 Ge'ez manuscripts. Jude 1:14-15 cites Enoch; Epistle of Barnabas 4:3 treats it as scripture; canonical for EOTC, Eritrean church and Beta Israel. Bruce 1773 three copies; Laurence 1821; Dillmann 1851; Charles 1906/1912.

Charles translation: 1:9 'And behold! He cometh with ten thousands of His holy ones'; 6:6 'two hundred; who descended in the days of Jared on the summit of Mount Hermon'; 8:1 'Azazel taught men to make swords'; 10:8 'to him ascribe all sin'; 14:20 'And the Great Glory sat thereon'.

Charles translation, Parables: 46:3 'This is the son of Man who hath righteousness'; 48:2-3 named before the Lord of Spirits before sun and signs were created; 62:7 'For from the beginning the Son of Man was hidden'; 71:14 'This is the Son of Man who is born unto righteousness'.
1 Enoch 94:8: 'Woe to you, you rich, for you have trusted in your riches' (paired with James 5:1).
Jude 14-15: Enoch 'in the seventh generation from Adam, prophesied' that the Lord comes with his holy ones 'to execute judgment upon all'.

entries.topic: Jubilees, Meqabyan, 4 Baruch and the broader-canon church-order books

claims.text: Jubilees prologue: 'This is the history of the division of the days of the law and of the testimony'; 1:26 'Write for Moses from the beginning of creation' (to the angel of the presence).

Jubilees: revealed by angels to Moses on Sinai; 49-year jubilees, fifty in all, 2,410 years creation to Sinai; 364-day calendar of four 13-week quarters, criticises lunar year; four classes of angels incl. angels of the presence; Watchers and Nephilim, a tenth of spirits left to lead people astray; Hebrew the language of heaven; c.160-150 BCE; about fifteen scrolls at Qumran from five caves; 50 chapters; complete only in Ge'ez, Latin covers about a quarter; canonical in EOTC, Eritrean church and among Beta Israel.

Jubilees teachings per JE: events written 'on the tablets of heaven'; rejects intercalated calendar 'in the strongest terms'; Mastema as Satan's name in the Passover account; Israel shares Sabbath and circumcision with the highest angels; festivals traced to Noah and patriarchs (Weeks first kept by Noah); separation from Gentiles; Noah's book of healing herbs.

Meqabyan: three books only in the Ethiopian canon, composed in Ge'ez, 'entirely different in their scope, content and subject' from Greek Maccabees; likely high-medieval; 1 Meqabyan: Benjaminite Maccabeus and sons Abijah, Shelah and Pantera refuse the idols of king Tseerutsaydan; later brothers revolt against Akrandis of Midian; themes resurrection, good works, vanity of power; chs 18-19 make Nephilim descendants of Cain's sons and Seth's daughters; 2 Meqabyan (21 chs): a Moabite-type Maccabeus who repents, taught by prophet Rei, strong bodily resurrection; 3 Meqabyan (10 chs): salvation and punishment, Devil was an angel punished for refusing to bow to Adam; English: Curtin and Tesfaye 2018/2023, Feqade Selassie 2008; BL Or. 506.

4 Baruch (Paralipomena of Jeremiah; Ge'ez 'Rest of the Words of Baruch'): Jeremiah hides vessels; Abimelech sleeps 66 years beside fresh figs; eagle carries Baruch's letter to Babylon and revives a corpse; return across the Jordan for those without foreign wives; usually dated first half of 2nd c. AD (AD 136 = 66 years after 70); Christian additions; canonical only in Ethiopia.

sources.label: R.H. Charles (tr.), The Book of Jubilees, prologue and ch.1, APOT (Oxford 1913), CCEL

entries.topic: Patristic doubts, Bruce 1773, Laurence 1821, Rome and Ethiopia

claims.text: Tertullian: some reject Enoch because it 'is not admitted into the Jewish canon either'; Noah could have preserved or renewed it; Enoch 'possesses a testimony in the Apostle Jude'.

Augustine: 'We cannot deny that Enoch, the seventh from Adam, left some divine writings'; 'their antiquity brought them under suspicion'; not in the canon 'preserved in the temple of the Hebrew people by the diligence of successive priests'; 'there is some truth in these apocryphal writings' but they have 'no canonical authority'.
Jerome on Jude: 'because in it he quotes from the apocryphal Book of Enoch it is rejected by many'.

Hessayon: Scaliger printed Greek excerpts of the Watchers from George Syncellus' 9th-c. chronography in 1606; Bruce found 1 Enoch manuscripts in Ethiopia 1773 (MS Bodl. Or. 531); Laurence translated one in 1821; rabbis and Fathers such as Athanasius and Augustine rejected the books. No suppression claim.

Chronology: Ludolf dismissed Peiresc's 'Enoch' manuscript; Bruce returned 1773 with three copies (Kinnaird, Bodleian, Royal Library Paris); de Sacy Latin of first chapters 1800; Laurence 1821 from the Bodleian copy, revised 1833/1838/1842; Dillmann Ethiopic text 1851, German 1853.

Mendes: Latin Patriarch from 1622, reached Fremona 21 June 1625; 11 February 1626 Susenyos and Mendes acknowledged Roman primacy, Catholicism state religion; Mendes condemned Saturday Sabbath and fasts, told women their children baptised in the Orthodox church were in hell; 14 June 1632 Susenyos rescinded the edict; Fasilides exiled Mendes 1634. No mention of the canon or Enoch.

Ethiopian Catholic Church: sui iuris Ge'ez-rite church in full communion with Rome; 1439 Eugene IV message to Zara Yaqob; De Jacobis prefect apostolic 1839; Pontifical Ethiopian College 1919; metropolitan province 20 February 1961; Eritrean Catholic Church separate January 2015; 70,832 members (2017).
